newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Airports report passenger, cargo traffic lift.
newsitem.headline: Airports report passenger, cargo traffic lift.

text.p: World airports Friday reported a 6.5 percent rise in passenger traffic in the first half of 1996, backing forecasts of strong growth for the airline industry to the end of the century.
Cargo traffic rose 4.5 percent in the six months through June from the year-earlier period.
Figures released by the Geneva-based Airports Council International (ACI) also showed that U.S. hubs held the top four places as the busiest passenger and cargo airports between January and June.

ACI, whose report was based on returns from 458 member airports around the globe, said 1.2 billion travellers passed through them in the first half of the year -- 73 million more than in the January-June period last year.

Chicago's O'Hare was the world's busiest passenger airport, seeing 33.5 million people pass through, followed by Atlanta where traffic in the first half was boosted 16.2 percent to 32.4 million due to the Olympic Games.

In third position was Los Angeles with 27.9 million passengers, followed by Dallas/Fort Worth with 27 million, London's Heathrow with 26.5 million and Tokyo's Haneda, Japan's main domestic hub, with 21.9 million.
Cargo moved totalled 23.3 million metric tons, 1 million tons more than last year, while aircraft movements were up two percent to 23.3 million.
ACI director-general Otis Dunham said the figures "lend support to recent airline forecasts of over 7 percent annual growth in passenger trafic through to the year 2000.
"This is very healthy growth, and all parties in the air transport industry must redouble their efforts to get more capacity out of the system."
This would imply "more efficient passenger and cargo processing, and the maximum use of new technologies both on the ground and in the air."
The largest percentage passenger growth this year, although from a low base, was recorded by ACI's Africa region which saw traffic climb by 7.7 percent to a total of 12.9 million passengers.

But North America, boosted by travel to the Olympic Games in Atlanta, saw growth of 7.1 percent for a total of 608.8 million. Asia/Pacific airports saw 6.9 percent more people passing through for a total of 168.7 million.

European region passengers were up 6.2 percent to a total of 330.3 million, while in the Middle East they totalled 21.7 million, an increase of 5.9 percent. Growth in Latin America and the Caribbean was only 1.7 percent to 36.5 million.

Top six cargo airports were Memphis, Tenn., which moved 915,057 tons, Los Angeles with 821,149 tons, Miami with 815,585, New York's Kennedy with 779,544, Tokyo's Narita with 771,045 and Germany's Frankfurt with 722,451 tons moved.
